title: indigo_mount_synscan: a failed auto home publishes OK before its ALERT, so the ALERT is not kept
description: Found on 2026-11-21 while working on ticket 3beb3554-f847-4155-b5e7-5bed700096f0 (closed, commit 296992891). mount_autohome_finish() (indigo_mount_synscan.driver about lines 1531-1533) publishes the coordinates OK through synscan_update_mount_coordinates() and then the failure ALERT, so the ALERT does not follow a BUSY and indigo_update_coordinates() does not keep it; on success the coordinates are published twice. Reproduce in the simulator suite, publish one result, add a *_keeps_alert case for a failed auto home. Bump the driver version; recorded simulator run.

outcome.summary:
Driver fix is correct; the new test synscan_mount_failed_autohome_keeps_alert is timing-dependent and fails about 1 run in 4.

Verified: mount_autohome_finish() now publishes exactly one coordinates result. On success there is one OK from synscan_update_mount_coordinates() (global_mode is already IDLE). On failure there is one ALERT through synscan_set_coordinate_state(); the polls before it were BUSY (global_mode HOMING), so update_coordinates() in indigo_libs/indigo_mount_driver.c:1393-1401 sets keep_coordinates_alert, and MOUNT_HORIZONTAL_COORDINATES follows in the same state (line 1409). MOUNT_AUTOHOME agrees on both paths. The abort and disconnect paths are unchanged and never reach mount_autohome_finish(): abort cancels the finalizer, disconnect sets home_stage IDLE first. No client values are rewritten. A scratch run of the unchanged generator reproduces the checked-in .c/.h/_main.c byte for byte. Version 27 -> 29 (0x0300001D). 119 cases registered, MIGRATION_STATUS 117 -> 119 with the Comment column untouched, and the record time fits the journal. Formatting is fine.

Defect: in a scratch copy, synscan_mount_failed_autohome_keeps_alert failed 4 of 16 runs at low load (load average 1.4-1.7), each time at test_mount_synscan_simulator.c:3992 'assertion failed: !synscan_fault_pending(&simulator)'. The simulator event log of a failing run shows why. motion_failure_keeps_alert() writes the ':f' fault about 2 s after the auto home starts. At that moment the auto home is often in HOME_PREP_REVERSE_INDEX: about 4 s of ':q1000000' index polling on RA, then the 3 s sensor-clearance dwell (delay = 3). Neither sends ':f'. The fixed 5 s wait (100 x 50 ms) ends before the next ':f' (HOME_PREP_DWELL -> HOME_WAIT), so the fault is still pending. The recorded 119/119 passed by chance.

Fix: make the failed-auto-home case independent of which stage is running when the fault is armed. For example, allow the auto home a fault-consumption wait longer than its longest phase withou

Re-review of 7fce21d16..d9e2abef9. The delta changes only tests, the simulator and record lines; the driver is unchanged at v29.

(1) Fix for the earlier finding: motion_failure_keeps_alert() now gives the auto home 600 x 50 ms = 30 s to consume the ':f' fault; the other motions keep 5 s. The fault is still armed while the auto home runs, so the case still proves the failure ALERT that follows BUSY and is kept by the polls. Scratch copy, 6 runs: 6/6 PASS, fault used after 5.1-5.7 s. That confirms the old 5 s bound sat at the edge and 30 s leaves ample margin.

(2) poll_failure_during_motion(): it first does an idle GoTo to HA 2 h / Dec 40, then takes the mark, then starts the 20 degree motion. The fixed 3.5 s sleep is replaced by synscan_wait_for_arrival(), which is bounded at 30 s and needs both @arrived1 and @arrived2 after the mark. This is event-driven. Arrivals from the preparatory GoTo fall before the mark: synscan_goto waits for the finalizer to see both axes stopped, and the simulator logs @arrived in the same timer tick that clears RUNNING. synscan_mark() and count_synscan_commands() both count every log line, so the indexes agree. What the cases prove is unchanged: wait_for_gate() still makes sure the single failed ':j2' poll happens and holds the queue, the failed poll must still be BUSY, every later coordinates publication must be OK with at least 2 OK polls, and MOUNT_HOME must end OK. Starting off the pole makes both moves 20 degrees, so the failed poll lands inside the motion more reliably than before. Scratch copy: goto/home_survives_a_failed_poll 2/2 PASS each.

Simulator: the @arrived<axis> line follows the existing @index pattern. The other readers of the event log are unaffected: they filter by ':' prefix or command, the handshake check reads lines before any GoTo, and the guider wire timing only sees tracking (no arrival).

Formatting follows AGENTS.md, git diff --check is clean, and README/TEST_SUMMARY change only the record line (17:29, 119/11

Review round 1 (changes) addressed, test/simulator only, driver stays v29. (1) synscan_mount_failed_autohome_keeps_alert: motion_failure_keeps_alert() now waits up to 30 s (auto home only; other motions keep 5 s) for the ':f' fault to be used, since the auto home sends no ':f' during home-index polling (~4 s) and the 3 s clearance dwell; measured consumption 5.0-5.9 s after arming in 20/20 consecutive passes (the old 5 s limit was marginal). (2) Coordinator addition: synscan_mount_goto_survives_a_failed_poll / synscan_mount_home_survives_a_failed_poll reproduced failing at 16:50 CET (extra BUSY poll). Cause: synscan_start_motion() starts from the pole of the date, where the J2000 raw coordinates are those of one fixed point whatever the RA axis position, so the hour angle it derives (LST - J2000 RA) follows the sidereal time; the RA move of the planned 20-degree motion varied with LST. One-off uncommitted sweep over 8 site longitudes (GEOGRAPHIC_COORDINATES, LST 2.4..23.4 h): old form RA move 27384..189157 steps (~11..79 deg, period 12 h), FAIL at 4 of 8 LSTs for both cases (moves >= 135k steps outlast the fixed 3.5 s sleep); new form RA move 47828..49125 steps (19.9..20.5 deg), PASS 16/16. Fix: poll_failure_during_motion() first slews to HA 2 h / Dec 40 (fixed axis move from the start position), then starts the 20-degree motion, and instead of the 3.5 s sleep waits until the simulator logs '@arrived1' and '@arrived2' (new physical-event lines in mount_synscan_simulator.c when a GoTo axis reaches its target). Recorded run: 2026-11-21 17:29 3.0.0.29 mac arm64 simulator 119/119 OK (with INDIGO_SIMULATOR_TRACE_DIR capture; no failures). Master gained b7083ad38 (ticket c3aeb19f, changes INDIGO_COPY_*_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE used by synscan) after this branch; not merged per instructions (merge only for 0b4af839), so the recorded run predates it.
